course_description:
This course will introduce the concepts of resource and reserve estimation in both coal and metalliferous deposits. This represents a critical component in the life cycle of a mine and provides the link between the processes of exploration geology and mine planning.

This course focuses on the principles and techniques for estimating the quantity and quality of mineral resources based on sample data taken from them. In doing so, this course lays the foundations and practical knowledge in geosciences, traditional resource estimation methods, geostatistics and block modelling which are required as the basis for the iterative strategic mine planning process and other more advanced courses in mining. This course provides opportunities to engage in reflective practices, critical evaluation, problem solving and risk management around compliance with the Joint Ore Reserves Committee (JORC) standard and the feasibility study process.

course_aims: The aim of this course is to introduce students to the principles of geology, deposit types and resource and reserve estimation for metalliferous and coal deposits as the basis from which to commence the mine planning process.

learning_outcomes.description: Illustrate the geoscientific processes in the formation of mineral deposits.
Communicate reserve and resource estimates according to the JORC standard.
Examine the error and risk in the orebody characterisation by applying the principles of sampling and compositing across drill samples
Apply traditional resource estimation techniques to the development of a resource estimate.
Collaborate as a team to develop a resource estimate using geostatistics with industry-standard software.
Defend the recommendation of further drilling locations that enhance confidence in orebody characterisation.

learning_activities.topic: Course introduction. Key aspects of mineral-rock relationships.
Earth processes: understanding the planet. The concept of an ore deposit.
Rock fabrics and orientations: geometric relations play a crucial role in the mining process.
Exploration geology regional and 'near-mine' exploration; geophysics and remote sensing.
Interpreting and displaying drill hole data.
The Mine Planning Process and Strategic Importance
